Problem 1 · Walk back from one known current

*Textbook P2.20*

The current $i_a$ is $2\,\mathrm{mA}$. Find **(a)** $i_o$, **(b)** $i_g$ and **(c)** the power delivered by the current source.

```schematic
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$i_g$"
R1 2,3 -> 2,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_o$"
R2 2,3 -> 5,3 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_a$"
R3 5,3 -> 5,0 "$4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" flip
R4 5,0 -> 2,0 "$3\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 0,3 -> 2,3
wire 2,0 -> 0,0
label 2,3 "$a$" above
label 5,3 "$b$" above
label 5,0 "$c$" right
label 0,0 "$d$" left
```

blocks.title: Show solution
blocks.text:
```circuitsteps
title "Problem 1 · Walk back from one known current"
== The circuit
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$i_g$"
R1 2,3 -> 2,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_o$"
R2 2,3 -> 5,3 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_a$"
R3 5,3 -> 5,0 "$4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" flip
R4 5,0 -> 2,0 "$3\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 0,3 -> 2,3
wire 2,0 -> 0,0
label 2,3 "$a$" above
label 5,3 "$b$" above
label 5,0 "$c$" right
label 0,0 "$d$" left
--
Only one number is given: $i_a=2\,\mathrm{mA}$.

Follow it: from $a$ it goes through the $1$, $4$ and $3\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ back to $d$.
== Same current down the chain
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$i_g$"
R1 2,3 -> 2,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_o$"
R2 2,3 -> 5,3 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_a$"
R3 5,3 -> 5,0 "$4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" flip
R4 5,0 -> 2,0 "$3\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 0,3 -> 2,3
wire 2,0 -> 0,0
label 2,3 "$a$" above
label 5,3 "$b$" above
label 5,0 "$c$" right
label 0,0 "$d$" left
#= path 2.3,3 -> 5,3 -> 5,0 -> 2.3,0 "$2\,\mathrm{mA}$" thin
--
$b$ and $c$ each join just **two** elements.

KCL at a two-element node: what comes in goes out.

So the $1$, $4$ and $3\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ all carry $2\,\mathrm{mA}$.
== Ohm's law on each
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$i_g$"
R1 2,3 -> 2,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_o$"
R2 2,3 -> 5,3 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_a$"
R3 5,3 -> 5,0 "$4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" flip
R4 5,0 -> 2,0 "$3\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 0,3 -> 2,3
wire 2,0 -> 0,0
label 2,3 "$a$" above
label 5,3 "$b$" above
label 5,0 "$c$" right
label 0,0 "$d$" left
#= sign 2.55,2.62 +
#= sign 4.45,2.62 -
#= sign 4.62,2.2 +
#= sign 4.62,0.8 -
#= sign 4.45,0.38 +
#= sign 2.55,0.38 -
#= text 3.5,2.2 "$2\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#= text 4.15,1.5 "$8\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#= text 3.5,0.8 "$6\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#+ $V_{1k}=2\,\mathrm{V}$
#+ $V_{4k}=8\,\mathrm{V}$
#+ $V_{3k}=6\,\mathrm{V}$
--
$+$ where the $2\,\mathrm{mA}$ **enters** each resistor.

- $1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$: $(2m)(1k)=2\,\mathrm{V}$
- $4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$: $(2m)(4k)=8\,\mathrm{V}$
- $3\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$: $(2m)(3k)=6\,\mathrm{V}$

$m\cdot k=1$, so the prefixes cancel.
== KVL around the right loop
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$i_g$"
R1 2,3 -> 2,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_o$"
R2 2,3 -> 5,3 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_a$"
R3 5,3 -> 5,0 "$4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" flip
R4 5,0 -> 2,0 "$3\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 0,3 -> 2,3
wire 2,0 -> 0,0
label 2,3 "$a$" above
label 5,3 "$b$" above
label 5,0 "$c$" right
label 0,0 "$d$" left
#= sign 2.55,2.62 +
#= sign 4.45,2.62 -
#= sign 4.62,2.2 +
#= sign 4.62,0.8 -
#= sign 4.45,0.38 +
#= sign 2.55,0.38 -
#= text 3.5,2.2 "$2\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#= text 4.15,1.5 "$8\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#= text 3.5,0.8 "$6\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#= sign 1.62,2.2 +
#= sign 1.62,0.8 -
#= path 2,3 -> 5,3 -> 5,0 -> 2,0 -> 2,2.3
#+ $V_{2k}=16\,\mathrm{V}$
--
Walk clockwise from $a$; write the sign you **enter** each element by:
- $1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$: enter $+$ → $+2$
- $4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$: enter $+$ → $+8$
- $3\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$: enter $+$ → $+6$
- $2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ (going up): enter $-$ → $-V_{2k}$

$$
2+8+6-V_{2k}=0 \;\Rightarrow\; V_{2k}=16\,\mathrm{V}
$$
== Ohm's law → $i_o$
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$i_g$"
R1 2,3 -> 2,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_o$"
R2 2,3 -> 5,3 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_a$"
R3 5,3 -> 5,0 "$4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" flip
R4 5,0 -> 2,0 "$3\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 0,3 -> 2,3
wire 2,0 -> 0,0
label 2,3 "$a$" above
label 5,3 "$b$" above
label 5,0 "$c$" right
label 0,0 "$d$" left
#= sign 1.62,2.2 +
#= sign 1.62,0.8 -
#= text 1.3,1.5 "$16\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#+ $i_o=8\,\mathrm{mA}$
--
The $2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ has $16\,\mathrm{V}$ across it, $+$ on top.

$$
i_o=\frac{16}{2k}=8\,\mathrm{mA}
$$

Positive: it flows down, the way its arrow points.
== KCL at $a$ → $i_g$
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$i_g$"
R1 2,3 -> 2,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_o$"
R2 2,3 -> 5,3 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_a$"
R3 5,3 -> 5,0 "$4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" flip
R4 5,0 -> 2,0 "$3\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 0,3 -> 2,3
wire 2,0 -> 0,0
label 2,3 "$a$" above
label 5,3 "$b$" above
label 5,0 "$c$" right
label 0,0 "$d$" left
#= text 1.3,1.5 "$16\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#= text 1,3.5 "$i_g=10\,\mathrm{mA}$" color=pink
#+ $i_g=10\,\mathrm{mA}$
--
Into $a$: $i_g$. Out of $a$: $i_o$ and $i_a$.

$$
i_g-i_o-i_a=0
$$

$$
i_g=8m+2m=10\,\mathrm{mA}
$$
== Power of the source
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$i_g$"
R1 2,3 -> 2,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_o$"
R2 2,3 -> 5,3 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_a$"
R3 5,3 -> 5,0 "$4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" flip
R4 5,0 -> 2,0 "$3\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 0,3 -> 2,3
wire 2,0 -> 0,0
label 2,3 "$a$" above
label 5,3 "$b$" above
label 5,0 "$c$" right
label 0,0 "$d$" left
#= text -0.95,0.85 "$160\,\mathrm{mW}$" color=green
#+ $p_g=160\,\mathrm{mW}$
--
The source sits between $d$ and $a$: $16\,\mathrm{V}$ across it, pushing $10\,\mathrm{mA}$ up into $a$.

$$
p_g=(16)(10m)=160\,\mathrm{mW}\ \text{delivered}
$$

**Check**, $V\cdot I$ for each resistor:

$$
(16)(8m)+(2)(2m)+(8)(2m)+(6)(2m)
$$

$$
=128+4+16+12=160\,\mathrm{mW}\ ✓
$$
```
Problem 2 · Split currents and check power

*Tutorial 1, P2.19*

Find $i_1$, $i_2$ and $v_o$, and check that the power balances.

```schematic
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$1.5\,\mathrm{A}$" v_rev="$v_o$"
wire 0,3 -> 4,3
wire 8,0 -> 0,0
R1 4,3 -> 4,0 "$100\,\Omega$" i="$i_1$"
R2 4,3 -> 8,3 "$150\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
R3 8,3 -> 8,0 "$250\,\Omega$"
```

blocks.title: Show solution
blocks.text:
```circuitsteps
title "Problem 2 · Split currents and check power"
== The circuit
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$1.5\,\mathrm{A}$" v_rev="$v_o$"
wire 0,3 -> 4,3
wire 8,0 -> 0,0
R1 4,3 -> 4,0 "$100\,\Omega$" i="$i_1$"
R2 4,3 -> 8,3 "$150\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
R3 8,3 -> 8,0 "$250\,\Omega$"
--
Find $i_1$, $i_2$ and $v_o$.

Two windows → two mesh currents.

The current source sits alone on the left edge.
== Mesh currents
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$1.5\,\mathrm{A}$" v_rev="$v_o$"
wire 0,3 -> 4,3
wire 8,0 -> 0,0
R1 4,3 -> 4,0 "$100\,\Omega$" i="$i_1$"
R2 4,3 -> 8,3 "$150\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
R3 8,3 -> 8,0 "$250\,\Omega$"
#= mesh 2,1.5 "$I_1$" cw r=0.7
#= mesh 5.9,1.5 "$I_2$" cw r=0.7
#+ $I_1=1.5\,\mathrm{A}$
--
$I_1$ and $I_2$, both clockwise.

The $1.5\,\mathrm{A}$ source is only in mesh 1 and points the same way as $I_1$:

$$
I_1=1.5\,\mathrm{A}
$$

No KVL for mesh 1: a current source has no fixed voltage.
== KVL around mesh 2
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$1.5\,\mathrm{A}$" v_rev="$v_o$"
wire 0,3 -> 4,3
wire 8,0 -> 0,0
R1 4,3 -> 4,0 "$100\,\Omega$" i="$i_1$"
R2 4,3 -> 8,3 "$150\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
R3 8,3 -> 8,0 "$250\,\Omega$"
#= mesh 2,1.5 "$I_1$" cw r=0.7
#= mesh 5.9,1.5 "$I_2$" cw r=0.7
#= sign 5.25,2.62 +
#= sign 6.75,2.62 -
#= sign 7.62,2.2 +
#= sign 7.62,0.8 -
#= sign 4.38,0.8 +
#= sign 4.38,2.2 -
#+ $I_2=0.3\,\mathrm{A}$
--
Mark $+$ where $I_2$ **enters** each resistor.

The $100\,\Omega$ is shared: in $I_2$'s direction it carries $I_2-I_1$.
- $150\,\Omega$: enter $+$ → $+150I_2$
- $250\,\Omega$: enter $+$ → $+250I_2$
- $100\,\Omega$: enter $+$ → $+100(I_2-I_1)$

$$
150I_2+250I_2+100(I_2-1.5)=0
$$

$$
500I_2=150 \;\Rightarrow\; I_2=0.3\,\mathrm{A}
$$
== Branch currents
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$1.5\,\mathrm{A}$" v_rev="$v_o$"
wire 0,3 -> 4,3
wire 8,0 -> 0,0
R1 4,3 -> 4,0 "$100\,\Omega$" i="$i_1$"
R2 4,3 -> 8,3 "$150\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
R3 8,3 -> 8,0 "$250\,\Omega$"
#= text 4.8,1.5 "$1.2\,\mathrm{A}$" color=pink
#= text 6,2.5 "$0.3\,\mathrm{A}$" color=pink
#+ $i_1=1.2\,\mathrm{A}$
#+ $i_2=0.3\,\mathrm{A}$
--
$i_2$ is only in mesh 2:

$$
i_2=I_2=0.3\,\mathrm{A}
$$

Down the $100\,\Omega$: $I_1$ goes down, $I_2$ goes up.

$$
i_1=I_1-I_2=1.5-0.3=1.2\,\mathrm{A}
$$
== Ohm's law → $v_o$
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$1.5\,\mathrm{A}$" v_rev="$v_o$"
wire 0,3 -> 4,3
wire 8,0 -> 0,0
R1 4,3 -> 4,0 "$100\,\Omega$" i="$i_1$"
R2 4,3 -> 8,3 "$150\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
R3 8,3 -> 8,0 "$250\,\Omega$"
#= text 4.8,1.5 "$1.2\,\mathrm{A}$" color=pink
#= text 6,2.5 "$0.3\,\mathrm{A}$" color=pink
#= sign 3.62,2.2 +
#= sign 3.62,0.8 -
#+ $v_o=120\,\mathrm{V}$
--
The source and the $100\,\Omega$ sit between the same top and bottom wires → same voltage.

$i_1$ enters the $100\,\Omega$ at the top → $+$ on top, same as $v_o$.

$$
v_o=i_1\cdot100=(1.2)(100)=120\,\mathrm{V}
$$
== Power check
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$1.5\,\mathrm{A}$" v_rev="$v_o$"
wire 0,3 -> 4,3
wire 8,0 -> 0,0
R1 4,3 -> 4,0 "$100\,\Omega$" i="$i_1$"
R2 4,3 -> 8,3 "$150\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
R3 8,3 -> 8,0 "$250\,\Omega$"
#= text -0.95,0.85 "$180\,\mathrm{W}$" color=green
#= text 4.85,1.5 "$144\,\mathrm{W}$" color=orange
#= text 6,2.5 "$13.5\,\mathrm{W}$" color=orange
#= text 8.95,1.5 "$22.5\,\mathrm{W}$" color=orange
#+ $p=180\,\mathrm{W}$
--
**Delivered** by the source (green):

$$
p=v_o\cdot1.5=(120)(1.5)=180\,\mathrm{W}
$$

**Absorbed**, $i^2R$ (orange):
- $100\,\Omega$: $(1.2)^2(100)=144\,\mathrm{W}$
- $150\,\Omega$: $(0.3)^2(150)=13.5\,\mathrm{W}$
- $250\,\Omega$: $(0.3)^2(250)=22.5\,\mathrm{W}$

$$
144+13.5+22.5=180\,\mathrm{W}\ ✓
$$
```
Problem 3 · Two circuits joined by one wire

*Tutorial 1, P2.35*

Find $i_o$ (the current in the wire joining the two networks), $i_1$ and $i_2$.

```schematic
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$18\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$12\,\Omega$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$6\,\Omega$" v="$v_\Delta$"
wire 3,0 -> 0,0
wire 3,0 -> 5,0
label 4,0 "$\leftarrow i_o$" below
G1 5,3 -> 5,0 "$\dfrac{v_\Delta}{2}$"
wire 5,3 -> 10,3
wire 5,0 -> 10,0
R3 7.5,3 -> 7.5,0 "$10\,\Omega$" i="$i_1$"
R4 10,3 -> 10,0 "$5\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
```

blocks.title: Show solution
blocks.text:
```circuitsteps
title "Problem 3 · Two circuits joined by one wire"
== The circuit
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$18\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$12\,\Omega$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$6\,\Omega$" v="$v_\Delta$"
wire 3,0 -> 0,0
wire 3,0 -> 5,0
label 4,0 "$\leftarrow i_o$" below
G1 5,3 -> 5,0 "$\dfrac{v_\Delta}{2}$"
wire 5,3 -> 10,3
wire 5,0 -> 10,0
R3 7.5,3 -> 7.5,0 "$10\,\Omega$" i="$i_1$"
R4 10,3 -> 10,0 "$5\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
--
Two networks touch through **one** wire.

Find $i_o$ in that wire, then $i_1$ and $i_2$.
== KCL around the left half
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$18\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$12\,\Omega$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$6\,\Omega$" v="$v_\Delta$"
wire 3,0 -> 0,0
wire 3,0 -> 5,0
label 4,0 "$\leftarrow i_o$" below
G1 5,3 -> 5,0 "$\dfrac{v_\Delta}{2}$"
wire 5,3 -> 10,3
wire 5,0 -> 10,0
R3 7.5,3 -> 7.5,0 "$10\,\Omega$" i="$i_1$"
R4 10,3 -> 10,0 "$5\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
#= region -1.3,-0.55 3.7,3.75 "left half" color=green
#= text 4,0.45 "$i_o=0$" color=pink
#+ $i_o=0$
--
Draw a box around the left half. Only **one** wire crosses it.

KCL for the whole box: what goes in must come out.

There is no second wire to bring current back, so

$$
i_o=0
$$

The wire only puts both bottoms at the same voltage.
== Left loop: mesh + KVL
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$18\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$12\,\Omega$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$6\,\Omega$" v="$v_\Delta$"
wire 3,0 -> 0,0
wire 3,0 -> 5,0
label 4,0 "$\leftarrow i_o$" below
G1 5,3 -> 5,0 "$\dfrac{v_\Delta}{2}$"
wire 5,3 -> 10,3
wire 5,0 -> 10,0
R3 7.5,3 -> 7.5,0 "$10\,\Omega$" i="$i_1$"
R4 10,3 -> 10,0 "$5\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
#= text 4,0.45 "$i_o=0$" color=pink
#= mesh 1.5,1.5 "$I$" cw r=0.7
#= sign 0.55,2.62 +
#= sign 2.45,2.62 -
#= sign 2.62,2.2 +
#= sign 2.62,0.8 -
#+ $I=1\,\mathrm{A}$
--
With $i_o=0$ the left side is one loop. Mesh current $I$, clockwise.

Sign you **enter** each element by:
- $18\,\mathrm{V}$: enter $-$ → $-18$
- $12\,\Omega$: enter $+$ → $+12I$
- $6\,\Omega$: enter $+$ → $+6I$

$$
-18+12I+6I=0 \;\Rightarrow\; I=1\,\mathrm{A}
$$
== Ohm's law → $v_\Delta$
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$18\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$12\,\Omega$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$6\,\Omega$" v="$v_\Delta$"
wire 3,0 -> 0,0
wire 3,0 -> 5,0
label 4,0 "$\leftarrow i_o$" below
G1 5,3 -> 5,0 "$\dfrac{v_\Delta}{2}$"
wire 5,3 -> 10,3
wire 5,0 -> 10,0
R3 7.5,3 -> 7.5,0 "$10\,\Omega$" i="$i_1$"
R4 10,3 -> 10,0 "$5\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
#= text 4,0.45 "$i_o=0$" color=pink
#= mesh 1.5,1.5 "$I$" cw r=0.7
#= text 2.2,1.5 "$6\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#+ $v_\Delta=6\,\mathrm{V}$
--
$I$ enters the $6\,\Omega$ at the top, the $+$ end of $v_\Delta$.

$$
v_\Delta=(6)(1)=6\,\mathrm{V}
$$
== The dependent source + KCL
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$18\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$12\,\Omega$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$6\,\Omega$" v="$v_\Delta$"
wire 3,0 -> 0,0
wire 3,0 -> 5,0
label 4,0 "$\leftarrow i_o$" below
G1 5,3 -> 5,0 "$\dfrac{v_\Delta}{2}$"
wire 5,3 -> 10,3
wire 5,0 -> 10,0
R3 7.5,3 -> 7.5,0 "$10\,\Omega$" i="$i_1$"
R4 10,3 -> 10,0 "$5\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
#= text 4,0.45 "$i_o=0$" color=pink
#= text 2.2,1.5 "$6\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#= text 5.75,1.5 "$3\,\mathrm{A}$" color=pink
#= region 4.6,2.6 10.4,3.4 "node" color=green
--
The diamond pulls $\dfrac{v_\Delta}{2}=\dfrac{6}{2}=3\,\mathrm{A}$ **down** out of the right top node.

KCL at that node (leaving $-$): $i_1$, $i_2$ and the $3\,\mathrm{A}$ all leave.

$$
-i_1-i_2-3=0 \;\Rightarrow\; i_1+i_2=-3
$$
== KVL around the right window
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$18\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$12\,\Omega$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$6\,\Omega$" v="$v_\Delta$"
wire 3,0 -> 0,0
wire 3,0 -> 5,0
label 4,0 "$\leftarrow i_o$" below
G1 5,3 -> 5,0 "$\dfrac{v_\Delta}{2}$"
wire 5,3 -> 10,3
wire 5,0 -> 10,0
R3 7.5,3 -> 7.5,0 "$10\,\Omega$" i="$i_1$"
R4 10,3 -> 10,0 "$5\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
#= text 4,0.45 "$i_o=0$" color=pink
#= text 5.75,1.5 "$3\,\mathrm{A}$" color=pink
#= path 7.5,1.6 -> 7.5,3 -> 10,3 -> 10,0 -> 7.5,0 -> 7.5,1.0
#= sign 9.62,2.2 +
#= sign 9.62,0.8 -
#= sign 7.88,2.2 +
#= sign 7.88,0.8 -
#+ $i_1=-1\,\mathrm{A}$
#+ $i_2=-2\,\mathrm{A}$
--
Walk clockwise: across the top, down the $5\,\Omega$, back, up the $10\,\Omega$.
- $5\,\Omega$: enter $+$ → $+5i_2$
- $10\,\Omega$ (going up): enter $-$ → $-10i_1$

$$
5i_2-10i_1=0 \;\Rightarrow\; i_2=2i_1
$$

Into the KCL:

$$
3i_1=-3 \;\Rightarrow\; i_1=-1\,\mathrm{A},\quad i_2=-2\,\mathrm{A}
$$

Negative: both really flow **up**, against their arrows.
```
Problem 4 · Balanced bridge and resistor ratings

*Assessment Problem 3.7*

The bridge is balanced (no galvanometer current). Find $R_x$, and check whether any resistor exceeds a $250\,\mathrm{mW}$ rating.

```schematic
V1 0,4 -> 0,0 "$5\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 0,4 -> 6,4
wire 6,0 -> 0,0
R1 3,4 -> 3,2 "$100\,\Omega$"
R3 3,2 -> 3,0 "$150\,\Omega$"
R2 6,4 -> 6,2 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R4 6,2 -> 6,0 "$R_x$"
AM1 3,2 -> 6,2 "galvanometer"
```

blocks.title: Show solution
blocks.text:
```circuitsteps
title "Problem 4 · Balanced bridge and resistor ratings"
== The circuit
V1 0,4 -> 0,0 "$5\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 0,4 -> 6,4
wire 6,0 -> 0,0
R1 3,4 -> 3,2 "$100\,\Omega$"
R3 3,2 -> 3,0 "$150\,\Omega$"
R2 6,4 -> 6,2 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R4 6,2 -> 6,0 "$R_x$"
AM1 3,2 -> 6,2 "galvanometer"
--
Find $R_x$.

**Balanced** = no current through the galvanometer.
== Balanced → take out the galvanometer
V1 0,4 -> 0,0 "$5\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 0,4 -> 6,4
wire 6,0 -> 0,0
R1 3,4 -> 3,2 "$100\,\Omega$"
R3 3,2 -> 3,0 "$150\,\Omega$"
R2 6,4 -> 6,2 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R4 6,2 -> 6,0 "$R_x$"
#= text 4.5,2.35 "$i_g=0$" color=accent
--
$i_g=0$, so removing the galvanometer changes nothing.

$i_g=0$ through it also means $0\,\mathrm{V}$ across it:

the two midpoints sit at the **same** voltage.
== Mesh current
V1 0,4 -> 0,0 "$5\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 0,4 -> 6,4
wire 6,0 -> 0,0
R1 3,4 -> 3,2 "$100\,\Omega$"
R3 3,2 -> 3,0 "$150\,\Omega$"
R2 6,4 -> 6,2 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R4 6,2 -> 6,0 "$R_x$"
#= mesh 1.5,2 "$I$" cw r=0.75
--
The left side is now one loop: $5\,\mathrm{V}$ → $100\,\Omega$ → $150\,\Omega$.

Give it a mesh current $I$, clockwise.
== Signs + KVL
V1 0,4 -> 0,0 "$5\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 0,4 -> 6,4
wire 6,0 -> 0,0
R1 3,4 -> 3,2 "$100\,\Omega$"
R3 3,2 -> 3,0 "$150\,\Omega$"
R2 6,4 -> 6,2 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R4 6,2 -> 6,0 "$R_x$"
#= mesh 1.5,2 "$I$" cw r=0.75
#= sign 2.65,3.6 +
#= sign 2.65,2.4 -
#= sign 2.65,1.6 +
#= sign 2.65,0.4 -
#+ $I=20\,\mathrm{mA}$
--
Signs you **enter** each element by:
- $5\,\mathrm{V}$: enter $-$ → $-5$
- $100\,\Omega$: enter $+$ → $+100I$
- $150\,\Omega$: enter $+$ → $+150I$

$$
-5+100I+150I=0
$$

$$
I=\frac{5}{250}=20\,\mathrm{mA}
$$
== Ohm's law on the $150\,\Omega$
V1 0,4 -> 0,0 "$5\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 0,4 -> 6,4
wire 6,0 -> 0,0
R1 3,4 -> 3,2 "$100\,\Omega$"
R3 3,2 -> 3,0 "$150\,\Omega$"
R2 6,4 -> 6,2 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R4 6,2 -> 6,0 "$R_x$"
#= text 3.75,1.0 "$3\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#+ $V_{150}=3\,\mathrm{V}$
--
$$
V_{150}=I\cdot150=(20m)(150)=3\,\mathrm{V}
$$

So the left midpoint is $3\,\mathrm{V}$ above the bottom wire.
== Same voltage on the right
V1 0,4 -> 0,0 "$5\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 0,4 -> 6,4
wire 6,0 -> 0,0
R1 3,4 -> 3,2 "$100\,\Omega$"
R3 3,2 -> 3,0 "$150\,\Omega$"
R2 6,4 -> 6,2 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R4 6,2 -> 6,0 "$R_x$"
#= text 3.75,1.0 "$3\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#= text 6.85,3.0 "$2\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#= text 6.85,1.0 "$3\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#= text 4.5,2.35 "$i_g=0$" color=accent
#+ $V_{R_x}=3\,\mathrm{V}$
--
$0\,\mathrm{V}$ across the galvanometer → the right midpoint is also $3\,\mathrm{V}$ up:

$$
V_{R_x}=3\,\mathrm{V}
$$

The right side spans the whole $5\,\mathrm{V}$:

$$
V_{1k}=5-3=2\,\mathrm{V}
$$
== Ohm's law → $R_x$
V1 0,4 -> 0,0 "$5\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 0,4 -> 6,4
wire 6,0 -> 0,0
R1 3,4 -> 3,2 "$100\,\Omega$"
R3 3,2 -> 3,0 "$150\,\Omega$"
R2 6,4 -> 6,2 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R4 6,2 -> 6,0 "$R_x$"
#= text 6.85,3.0 "$2\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#= text 6.85,1.0 "$3\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#+ $I_{right}=2\,\mathrm{mA}$
#+ $R_x=1.5\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$
--
Current down the right side:

$$
I_{right}=\frac{2}{1k}=2\,\mathrm{mA}
$$

Same current through $R_x$:

$$
R_x=\frac{3}{2m}=1.5\,\mathrm{k\Omega}
$$

Check (balance rule $R_1R_x=R_2R_3$): $R_x=\dfrac{(1k)(150)}{100}=1.5\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ ✓

$$
\boxed{R_x=1.5\,\mathrm{k\Omega}}
$$
== Power ratings
V1 0,4 -> 0,0 "$5\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 0,4 -> 6,4
wire 6,0 -> 0,0
R1 3,4 -> 3,2 "$100\,\Omega$"
R3 3,2 -> 3,0 "$150\,\Omega$"
R2 6,4 -> 6,2 "$1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R4 6,2 -> 6,0 "$R_x$"
#= text 3.85,3.0 "$40\,\mathrm{mW}$" color=orange
#= text 3.85,1.0 "$60\,\mathrm{mW}$" color=orange
#= text 6.9,3.0 "$4\,\mathrm{mW}$" color=orange
#= text 6.9,1.0 "$6\,\mathrm{mW}$" color=orange

--
$p=VI$ for each resistor:
- $100\,\Omega$: $(2)(20m)=40\,\mathrm{mW}$
- $150\,\Omega$: $(3)(20m)=60\,\mathrm{mW}$
- $1\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$: $(2)(2m)=4\,\mathrm{mW}$
- $R_x$: $(3)(2m)=6\,\mathrm{mW}$

Largest: $60\,\mathrm{mW}<250\,\mathrm{mW}$ → **no resistor exceeds its rating**.
```

```circuitsteps
title "Problem 5 · A triangle with no series or parallel pairs"
== The circuit
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$2\,\mathrm{A}$" v_rev="$v$"
wire 0,3 -> 0,5
R1 0,5 -> 8,5 "$28\,\Omega$"
wire 8,5 -> 8,3
R2 0,3 -> 4,3 "$20\,\Omega$"

R4 4,3 -> 4,0 "$5\,\Omega$"
R5 8,3 -> 8,0 "$105\,\Omega$"
wire 0,0 -> 4,0
wire 4,0 -> 8,0
--
Find $v$, the voltage across the $2\,\mathrm{A}$ source.

$v=(2\,\mathrm{A})(R_{in})$, so we need the resistance the source sees.

No two resistors are in series or in parallel.
== Spot the Δ
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$2\,\mathrm{A}$" v_rev="$v$"
wire 0,3 -> 0,5
R1 0,5 -> 8,5 "$28\,\Omega$"
wire 8,5 -> 8,3
R2 0,3 -> 4,3 "$20\,\Omega$"
R3 4,3 -> 8,3 "$10\,\Omega$"
R4 4,3 -> 4,0 "$5\,\Omega$"
R5 8,3 -> 8,0 "$105\,\Omega$"
wire 0,0 -> 4,0
wire 4,0 -> 8,0
label 0,4 "$a$" right
label 4,3 "$b$" above
label 8,4 "$c$" left
#= region -0.75,2.55 8.3,5.75 "Δ"
--
$28\,\Omega$, $20\,\Omega$ and $10\,\Omega$ form a triangle between $a$, $b$ and $c$.

That triangle (Δ) is what blocks every series/parallel move.
== Δ → Y
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$2\,\mathrm{A}$" v_rev="$v$"
wire 0,3 -> 0,5
RA 0,5 -> 4,5 "$9.66\,\Omega$"
RC 4,5 -> 8,5 "$4.83\,\Omega$"
wire 8,5 -> 8,3
RB 4,5 -> 4,3 "$3.45\,\Omega$"
R4 4,3 -> 4,0 "$5\,\Omega$"
R5 8,3 -> 8,0 "$105\,\Omega$"
wire 0,0 -> 4,0
wire 4,0 -> 8,0
label 0,4 "$a$" right
label 4,3 "$b$" right
label 8,4 "$c$" left
label 4,5 "$n$" above
#+ $R_{an}=9.66\,\Omega$
#+ $R_{bn}=3.45\,\Omega$
#+ $R_{cn}=4.83\,\Omega$
--
Same three corners $a$, $b$, $c$; new centre node $n$.

Each arm = (the two Δ resistors touching that corner) ÷ (sum).

Sum: $28+20+10=58\,\Omega$

$$
R_{an}=\frac{(28)(20)}{58}=\frac{280}{29}\approx9.66\,\Omega
$$

$$
R_{bn}=\frac{(20)(10)}{58}=\frac{100}{29}\approx3.45\,\Omega
$$

$$
R_{cn}=\frac{(28)(10)}{58}=\frac{140}{29}\approx4.83\,\Omega
$$
== Series pairs
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$2\,\mathrm{A}$" v_rev="$v$"
wire 0,3 -> 0,5
RA 0,5 -> 4,5 "$9.66\,\Omega$"
RBS 4,5 -> 4,0 "$8.45\,\Omega$"
wire 4,5 -> 8,5
RCS 8,5 -> 8,0 "$109.83\,\Omega$"
wire 0,0 -> 4,0
wire 4,0 -> 8,0
label 4,5 "$n$" above
#+ $R_b=8.45\,\Omega$
#+ $R_c=109.83\,\Omega$
--
From $n$ down to the bottom wire there are now two paths.

Through $b$: $R_{bn}$ and $5\,\Omega$ in series.

$$
R_b=3.45+5=8.45\,\Omega
$$

Through $c$: $R_{cn}$ and $105\,\Omega$ in series.

$$
R_c=4.83+105=109.83\,\Omega
$$
== Parallel pair
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$2\,\mathrm{A}$" v_rev="$v$"
wire 0,3 -> 0,5
RA 0,5 -> 4,5 "$9.66\,\Omega$"
RP 4,5 -> 4,0 "$7.84\,\Omega$"
wire 0,0 -> 4,0
label 4,5 "$n$" above
#+ $R_p=7.84\,\Omega$
--
Both paths run from $n$ to the bottom wire → parallel.

$$
R_p=\frac{(8.45)(109.83)}{8.45+109.83}\approx7.84\,\Omega
$$
== Series → $R_{in}$
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$2\,\mathrm{A}$" v_rev="$v$"
wire 0,3 -> 0,5
wire 0,5 -> 4,5
RIN 4,5 -> 4,0 "$17.5\,\Omega$"
wire 0,0 -> 4,0
#+ $R_{in}=17.5\,\Omega$
--
$R_{an}$ and $R_p$ are in series:

$$
R_{in}=9.66+7.84=17.5\,\Omega
$$

(Exactly $17.5$ with the fractions.)
== Ohm's law → $v$
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$2\,\mathrm{A}$" v_rev="$v$"
wire 0,3 -> 0,5
wire 0,5 -> 4,5
RIN 4,5 -> 4,0 "$17.5\,\Omega$"
wire 0,0 -> 4,0
#= mesh 1.6,2.5 "$2\,\mathrm{A}$" cw r=0.7
#= sign 4.38,3.2 +
#= sign 4.38,1.8 -
#+ $v=35\,\mathrm{V}$
--
One loop: the source forces $2\,\mathrm{A}$ through $R_{in}$.

$2\,\mathrm{A}$ enters $R_{in}$ at the top → $+$ on top, same as $v$.

$$
v=(2)(17.5)=35\,\mathrm{V}
$$

$$
\boxed{v=35\,\mathrm{V}}
$$
```

```circuitsteps
**Method: nodal.** Only 3 unknown nodes ($a$, $b$, $c$), and the current source just feeds $1\,\mathrm{A}$ into $a$.

- Nodes $a$, $b$, $c$ → $V_a$, $V_b$, $V_c$.
- Bottom wire = ground = $0\,\mathrm{V}$.

label 6,3 "$b$" above
label 9,3 "$c$" right

--
Every resistor current points down to ground, or from the higher node to the lower one ($a$ is fed by the source, so $a \to b \to c$).

Current $=$ (start − end) $/R$.

KCL: leaving $-$, entering $+$.
== KCL at $a$
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$1\,\mathrm{A}$"
R1 3,3 -> 3,0 "$240\,\Omega$" i
R2 3,3 -> 6,3 "$20\,\Omega$" i
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$100\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
R4 6,3 -> 9,3 "$50\,\Omega$" i

ground 0,0
#= region -0.4,2.6 3.4,5.4 color=green

$1\,\mathrm{A}$ enters; three currents leave.

$$
+1-\frac{V_a-0}{240}-\frac{V_a-V_b}{20}-\frac{V_a-V_c}{320}=0
$$

Multiply by $-960$:

$$
55V_a-48V_b-3V_c=960
$$
== KCL at $b$

label 9,3 "$c$" right
ground 0,0
#= region 5.55,2.55 6.45,3.45 color=green
--
$$
+\frac{V_a-V_b}{20}-\frac{V_b-0}{100}-\frac{V_b-V_c}{50}=0
$$

Multiply by $100$:

$$
5V_a-8V_b+2V_c=0
$$
== KCL at $c$

label 9,3 "$c$" right

#= region 8.55,2.6 9.45,5.4 color=green
--
$$
+\frac{V_b-V_c}{50}+\frac{V_a-V_c}{320}-\frac{V_c-0}{600}=0
$$

Multiply by $4800$:

$$
15V_a+96V_b-119V_c=0
$$
== Solve the node voltages
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$1\,\mathrm{A}$"
R1 3,3 -> 3,0 "$240\,\Omega$" i
R2 3,3 -> 6,3 "$20\,\Omega$" i
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$100\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"

#+ $V_b=60\,\mathrm{V}$

From $b$:

$$
V_b=\tfrac58V_a+\tfrac14V_c
$$

Into $c$: $75V_a-95V_c=0$, so

$$
V_c=\tfrac{15}{19}V_a \qquad V_b=\tfrac{125}{152}V_a
$$

Into $a$:

$$
\tfrac{250}{19}V_a=960 \;\Rightarrow\; V_a=72.96\,\mathrm{V}
$$

$$
V_b=60\,\mathrm{V} \qquad V_c=57.6\,\mathrm{V}
$$
== Ohm's law → $i_o$, $i_1$, $i_2$
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$1\,\mathrm{A}$"
R1 3,3 -> 3,0 "$240\,\Omega$" i
R2 3,3 -> 6,3 "$20\,\Omega$" i

R5 9,3 -> 9,0 "$600\,\Omega$" i="$i_o$"

wire 0,3 -> 3,3
wire 3,3 -> 3,5
wire 9,5 -> 9,3
wire 9,0 -> 0,0

label 6,3 "$b$" above
label 9,3 "$c$" right
ground 0,0
#= text 1.6,4.3 "$72.96\,\mathrm{V}$" color=green
#= text 6,4.15 "$60\,\mathrm{V}$" color=green
#= text 10.4,4.15 "$57.6\,\mathrm{V}$" color=green

#+ $i_o=0.096\,\mathrm{A}$

#+ $i_2=0.6\,\mathrm{A}$
--
$$
i_o=\frac{V_c-0}{600}=\frac{57.6}{600}=0.096\,\mathrm{A}
$$

$$
i_1=\frac{V_a-V_c}{320}=\frac{15.36}{320}=0.048\,\mathrm{A}
$$

$$
i_2=\frac{V_b-0}{100}=\frac{60}{100}=0.6\,\mathrm{A}
$$
== Power of the source
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$1\,\mathrm{A}$"
R1 3,3 -> 3,0 "$240\,\Omega$" i
R2 3,3 -> 6,3 "$20\,\Omega$" i
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$100\,\Omega$" i="$i_2$"
R4 6,3 -> 9,3 "$50\,\Omega$" i
R5 9,3 -> 9,0 "$600\,\Omega$" i="$i_o$"
R6 3,5 -> 9,5 "$320\,\Omega$" i="$i_1$"
wire 0,3 -> 3,3
wire 3,3 -> 3,5
wire 9,5 -> 9,3
wire 9,0 -> 0,0
label 3,5 "$a$" left
label 6,3 "$b$" above
label 9,3 "$c$" right
ground 0,0
#= text 1.6,4.3 "$72.96\,\mathrm{V}$" color=green

--
The source pushes $1\,\mathrm{A}$ up from ground ($0\,\mathrm{V}$) into $a$ ($72.96\,\mathrm{V}$): it lifts the current, so it **delivers**.

$$
p=V_a\cdot 1=72.96\cdot 1
$$

$$
\boxed{p=72.96\,\mathrm{W}\text{ delivered}}
$$
```

```circuitsteps
$$
\boxed{p=2.912\,\mathrm{mW}}
$$
```

```circuitsteps
$$
\boxed{v_o=45i=45(-3)=-135\,\mathrm{V}}

== Back to the original circuit
I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$5\,\mathrm{A}$"
R1 0,3 -> 2.5,3 "$8\,\Omega$"

The $5$, $45$, $10\,\Omega$ were never touched → they still carry $i=-3\,\mathrm{A}$.

V_q=340+5i+45i+10i=340-180=160\,\mathrm{V}

I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$5\,\mathrm{A}$"

$$
i_{340}=-3-4.25=-7.25\,\mathrm{A}\ (q\to r)

So $7.25\,\mathrm{A}$ flows $r\to q$ through the source: out of its $+$ → it **delivers**

$$
```

blocks.text:
```circuitsteps
title "Problem 13 · Thévenin: one equivalent, any load"
== The circuit
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$200\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$25\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$75\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 3,3 -> 5,3
wire 0,0 -> 5,0
terminal 5,3
terminal 5,0
wire 5,3 -> 7,3
R3 7,3 -> 7,0 "$R_L$"
wire 5,0 -> 7,0
gap 5,3 -> 5,0 v="$v_o$"
--
$R_L$ sits across the output terminals → it's the **load**.

**Plan**
1. Pull out $R_L$ → Thévenin equivalent ($V_{Th}$, $R_{Th}$).
2. (a), (b): put each load on the Thévenin circuit.
3. (c), (d): these ask about resistors **inside** → back to the original circuit.
== Pull out the load
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$200\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$25\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$75\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 3,3 -> 5,3
wire 0,0 -> 5,0
terminal 5,3
terminal 5,0
gap 5,3 -> 5,0 v="$V_{oc}$"
--
$R_L$ is gone → the terminals are **open**.

The voltage across them is $V_{oc}=V_{Th}$.
== Mesh current
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$200\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$25\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$75\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 3,3 -> 5,3
wire 0,0 -> 5,0
terminal 5,3
terminal 5,0
gap 5,3 -> 5,0 v="$V_{oc}$"
#= mesh 1.25,1.5 "$I$" cw r=0.6
#= sign 0.6,2.65 +
#= sign 2.4,2.65 -
#= sign 3.35,2.3 +
#= sign 3.35,0.7 -
#+ $I=2\,\mathrm{mA}$
--
One loop. $+$ where $I$ **enters** each resistor.

KVL (sign you enter by):

$$
-200+25kI+75kI=0
$$

$$
100kI=200 \;\Rightarrow\; I=2\,\mathrm{mA}
$$
== Ohm → $V_{oc}$
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$200\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$25\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$75\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 3,3 -> 5,3
wire 0,0 -> 5,0
terminal 5,3
terminal 5,0
gap 5,3 -> 5,0 v="$V_{oc}$"
#= sign 0.6,2.65 +
#= sign 2.4,2.65 -
#= sign 3.35,2.3 +
#= sign 3.35,0.7 -
#= path 4.8,3 -> 3,3 -> 3,0 -> 4.7,0
#+ $V_{Th}=150\,\mathrm{V}$
--
Walk from the $+$ terminal to the $-$ terminal: down the $75\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$, entering $+$.

$$
V_{oc}=I\cdot 75k=(2m)(75k)=150\,\mathrm{V}
$$

**(a)** No load → $v_o=V_{oc}$:

$$
\boxed{v_o=150\,\mathrm{V}}
$$
== $R_{Th}$: source off
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$25\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 0,3 -> 0,0
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$75\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 3,3 -> 5,3
wire 0,0 -> 5,0
terminal 5,3
terminal 5,0
#= path 6.6,1.5 -> 5.25,1.5 thin color=accent
#= text 6,1.95 "$R_{Th}$" color=accent
#+ $R_{Th}=18.75\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$
--
Voltage source off → **wire**.

From the terminals, $25\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ and $75\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ both go from the top wire to the bottom wire → **parallel**:

$$
R_{Th}=\frac{(25k)(75k)}{25k+75k}=\frac{1875M}{100k}=18.75\,\mathrm{k\Omega}
$$
== (b) Thévenin circuit + $150\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$
VTH 0,3 -> 0,0 "$150\,\mathrm{V}$"
RTH 0,3 -> 3,3 "$18.75\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 3,3 -> 5,3
wire 0,0 -> 5,0
terminal 5,3
terminal 5,0
wire 5,3 -> 7,3
R3 7,3 -> 7,0 "$150\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 5,0 -> 7,0
gap 5,3 -> 5,0 v="$v_o$"
#= mesh 3.25,1.5 "$I_b$" cw r=0.8
#= sign 0.6,2.65 +
#= sign 2.4,2.65 -
#= sign 7.35,2.3 +
#= sign 7.35,0.7 -
#+ $v_o=133.33\,\mathrm{V}$ (b)
--
$V_{Th}$ in series with $R_{Th}$; the $150\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ load on the terminals.

KVL:

$$
-150+18.75kI_b+150kI_b=0
$$

$$
I_b=\frac{150}{168.75k}=0.889\,\mathrm{mA}
$$

Ohm on the load:

$$
v_o=I_b\cdot150k=\frac{150}{168.75k}(150k)
$$

$$
\boxed{v_o=133.33\,\mathrm{V}}
$$
== (c) Load terminals shorted
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$200\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$25\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$75\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 3,3 -> 5,3
wire 0,0 -> 5,0
terminal 5,3
terminal 5,0
wire 5,3 -> 5,0
#= mesh 1.25,1.5 "$I_c$" cw r=0.6
#= sign 0.6,2.65 +
#= sign 2.4,2.65 -
#+ $p_{25k}=1.6\,\mathrm{W}$ (c)
--
The $25\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ is **inside** the equivalent → back to the original circuit.

The short sits across the $75\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ → it carries no current.

KVL (left loop):

$$
-200+25kI_c=0 \;\Rightarrow\; I_c=8\,\mathrm{mA}
$$

Check: $V_{Th}/R_{Th}=150/18.75k=8\,\mathrm{mA}$ ✓

$$
p=I_c^2\cdot25k=(8m)^2(25k)=(64\mu)(25k)
$$

$$
\boxed{p_{25k}=1.6\,\mathrm{W}}
$$
== (d) Most power in the $75\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$200\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$25\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$75\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 3,3 -> 5,3
wire 0,0 -> 5,0
terminal 5,3
terminal 5,0
gap 5,3 -> 5,0 v="$V_{oc}$"
#= mesh 1.25,1.5 "$I$" cw r=0.6
#= sign 3.35,2.3 +
#= sign 3.35,0.7 -
#+ $p_{75k,\max}=0.3\,\mathrm{W}$ (d)
--
$p_{75k}=v_o^2/75k$ → largest when $v_o$ is largest.

Any load pulls $v_o$ below $V_{Th}$ ($v_o=150\cdot\frac{R_L}{18.75k+R_L}<150$) → **no load** is the worst case.

No load: $I=2\,\mathrm{mA}$ (step 3).

$$
p=I^2\cdot75k=(2m)^2(75k)=(4\mu)(75k)
$$

$$
\boxed{p_{75k,\max}=0.3\,\mathrm{W}}
$$
```

blocks.text:
```circuitsteps
title "Problem 14 · Thévenin"
== The circuit
R1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
V1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$6\,\mathrm{V}$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
V2 6,3 -> 3,3 "$12\,\mathrm{V}$"
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 6,3 -> 8,3
wire 0,0 -> 8,0
terminal 8,3
terminal 8,0
gap 8,3 -> 8,0 v="$V_o$"
--
Find $V_o$: the voltage across the right $2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$.

That $2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ sits right across the output → it's the **load** $R_L$.

**Plan**
1. Pull out $R_L$.
2. $V_{Th}=V_{oc}$ with mesh + Ohm's law.
3. $R_{Th}$: sources off.
4. Put $R_L$ back on the Thévenin circuit.
== Pull out the load
R1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
V1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$6\,\mathrm{V}$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
V2 6,3 -> 3,3 "$12\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 6,3 -> 8,3
wire 0,0 -> 8,0
terminal 8,3
terminal 8,0
gap 8,3 -> 8,0 v="$V_{oc}$"
--
$R_L$ is gone → the terminals are **open**.

The voltage across them is $V_{oc}=V_{Th}$.

Open terminals → **no current** in the $12\,\mathrm{V}$ branch.
== Mesh current
R1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
V1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$6\,\mathrm{V}$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
V2 6,3 -> 3,3 "$12\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 6,3 -> 8,3
wire 0,0 -> 8,0
terminal 8,3
terminal 8,0
gap 8,3 -> 8,0 v="$V_{oc}$"
#= mesh 1.5,1.5 "$I_1$" ccw r=0.75
--
Only one closed loop is left: $2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ → $6\,\mathrm{V}$ → $4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$.

Give it a mesh current $I_1$ (counter-clockwise here; either way works).
== Signs + KVL
R1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
V1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$6\,\mathrm{V}$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
V2 6,3 -> 3,3 "$12\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 6,3 -> 8,3
wire 0,0 -> 8,0
terminal 8,3
terminal 8,0
gap 8,3 -> 8,0 v="$V_{oc}$"
#= mesh 1.5,1.5 "$I_1$" ccw r=0.75
#= sign 0.35,2.3 +
#= sign 0.35,0.7 -
#= sign 2.65,0.7 +
#= sign 2.65,2.3 -
#+ $I_1=1\,\mathrm{mA}$
--
Mark $+$ where $I_1$ **enters** each resistor.

Walk the loop with $I_1$; write the sign you **enter** each element by:
- $4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$: enter $+$ → $+4kI_1$
- $6\,\mathrm{V}$: enter $-$ → $-6$
- $2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$: enter $+$ → $+2kI_1$

$$
4kI_1-6+2kI_1=0
$$

$$
6kI_1=6 \;\Rightarrow\; I_1=\frac{6}{6k}=1\,\mathrm{mA}
$$
== Ohm's law on the $2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$
R1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
V1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$6\,\mathrm{V}$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
V2 6,3 -> 3,3 "$12\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 6,3 -> 8,3
wire 0,0 -> 8,0
terminal 8,3
terminal 8,0
gap 8,3 -> 8,0 v="$V_{oc}$"
#= mesh 1.5,1.5 "$I_1$" ccw r=0.75
#= sign 0.35,2.3 +
#= sign 0.35,0.7 -
#= text 1.1,1.5 "$2\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#+ $V_{2k}=2\,\mathrm{V}$
--
$$
V_{2k}=I_1\cdot 2k=(1m)(2k)=2\,\mathrm{V}
$$

$m\cdot k=1$, so the prefixes cancel.

$+$ is on top (where $I_1$ enters).
== KVL walk to $V_{oc}$
R1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
V1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$6\,\mathrm{V}$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
V2 6,3 -> 3,3 "$12\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 6,3 -> 8,3
wire 0,0 -> 8,0
terminal 8,3
terminal 8,0
gap 8,3 -> 8,0 v="$V_{oc}$"
#= sign 0.35,2.3 +
#= sign 0.35,0.7 -
#= text 1.1,1.5 "$2\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#= path 7.75,3 -> 0,3 -> 0,0 -> 7.7,0
#+ $V_{Th}=8\,\mathrm{V}$
--
Walk from the $+$ terminal to the $-$ terminal. Same rule: the sign you **enter** each element by.
- $12\,\mathrm{V}$: enter $+$ → $+12$
- $6\,\mathrm{V}$: enter $-$ → $-6$
- $2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$: enter $+$ → $+2$

$$
V_{oc}=12-6+2=8\,\mathrm{V}
$$

$$
\boxed{V_{Th}=8\,\mathrm{V}}
$$
== $R_{Th}$: sources off
R1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 0,3 -> 3,3
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 3,3 -> 6,3
wire 6,3 -> 8,3
wire 0,0 -> 8,0
terminal 8,3
terminal 8,0
#= path 9.6,1.5 -> 8.25,1.5 thin color=accent
#= text 9.1,1.95 "$R_{Th}$" color=accent
#+ $R_{Th}=\tfrac43\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$
--
Voltage source off = **short** (a wire).

Looking in from the terminals: $2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ and $4\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ both span the top wire to the bottom wire → **parallel**.

$$
R_{Th}=\frac{(2k)(4k)}{2k+4k}=\frac{8k^2}{6k}=\tfrac{4}{3}\,\mathrm{k\Omega}
$$
== Thévenin circuit + load back
VTH 0,3 -> 0,0 "$8\,\mathrm{V}$"
RTH 0,3 -> 3,3 "$\tfrac{4}{3}\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 3,3 -> 6,3
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 6,3 -> 8,3
wire 0,0 -> 8,0
terminal 8,3
terminal 8,0
gap 8,3 -> 8,0 v="$V_o$"
--
$V_{Th}=8\,\mathrm{V}$ in series with $R_{Th}=\tfrac43\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$.

$R_L=2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ is back. One loop again → mesh.
== Mesh + Ohm → $V_o$
VTH 0,3 -> 0,0 "$8\,\mathrm{V}$"
RTH 0,3 -> 3,3 "$\tfrac{4}{3}\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 3,3 -> 6,3
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 6,3 -> 8,3
wire 0,0 -> 8,0
terminal 8,3
terminal 8,0
gap 8,3 -> 8,0 v="$V_o$"
#= mesh 3,1.5 "$I$" cw r=0.8
#= sign 0.65,2.62 +
#= sign 2.35,2.62 -
#= sign 5.65,2.3 +
#= sign 5.65,0.7 -
#+ $I=2.4\,\mathrm{mA}$
#+ $V_o=4.8\,\mathrm{V}$
--
KVL with $I$ (signs you enter by):

$$
-8+\tfrac43kI+2kI=0
$$

$$
\tfrac{10}{3}kI=8 \;\Rightarrow\; I=\frac{8}{\tfrac{10}{3}k}=2.4\,\mathrm{mA}
$$

Ohm's law on $R_L$:

$$
V_o=I\cdot 2k=(2.4m)(2k)
$$

$$
\boxed{V_o=4.8\,\mathrm{V}}
$$
```

```circuitsteps
title "Problem 16 · Thévenin by source transformations, then a voltmeter"
== The circuit
V1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$36\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3.5,3 "$12\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
I1 3.5,0 -> 3.5,3 "$18\,\mathrm{mA}$" flip
wire 3.5,3 -> 6,3
R2 6,3 -> 6,0 "$60\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" flip

label 9,0 "$B$" below
gap 9,3 -> 9,0 v="$v_{AB}$"
--
The voltmeter goes on $A$, $B$ → it is the **load**: a $100\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ resistor.

**Plan**
1. Source transformations until one source and one resistor are left: that's the Thévenin circuit.
2. Put the $100\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ meter on it → mesh + Ohm.
== $36\,\mathrm{V}$ + $12\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ → current source
IA 0,3 -> 0,0 "$3\,\mathrm{mA}$"
wire 0,3 -> 6,3
R1 1.5,3 -> 1.5,0 "$12\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" flip
I1 3.5,0 -> 3.5,3 "$18\,\mathrm{mA}$" flip
R2 6,3 -> 6,0 "$60\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" flip
R3 6,3 -> 9,3 "$15\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 0,0 -> 9,0
terminal 9,3
terminal 9,0
label 9,3 "$A$" above
label 9,0 "$B$" below
gap 9,3 -> 9,0 v="$v_{AB}$"
--
The $36\,\mathrm{V}$ source and $12\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ are in **series** → swap for a current source **parallel** with $12\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$.

$$
i=\frac{36}{12k}=3\,\mathrm{mA}
$$

Direction: the source pushes current out of its $+$ end. $+$ is at the **bottom** → the arrow points **down**.
== Add the current sources
IA 0,0 -> 0,3 "$15\,\mathrm{mA}$"
wire 0,3 -> 6,3
R1 1.5,3 -> 1.5,0 "$12\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" flip
R2 6,3 -> 6,0 "$60\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" flip
R3 6,3 -> 9,3 "$15\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 0,0 -> 9,0
terminal 9,3
terminal 9,0
label 9,3 "$A$" above
label 9,0 "$B$" below
gap 9,3 -> 9,0 v="$v_{AB}$"
--
$3\,\mathrm{mA}$ down and $18\,\mathrm{mA}$ up, between the same two wires → add them (up $+$):

$$
-3m+18m=15\,\mathrm{mA} \text{ up}
$$
== Combine the parallel resistors
IA 0,0 -> 0,3 "$15\,\mathrm{mA}$"
wire 0,3 -> 6,3
R2 6,3 -> 6,0 "$10\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" flip
R3 6,3 -> 9,3 "$15\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 0,0 -> 9,0
terminal 9,3
terminal 9,0
label 9,3 "$A$" above
label 9,0 "$B$" below
gap 9,3 -> 9,0 v="$v_{AB}$"
--
$12\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ and $60\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ both span the top and bottom wires → **parallel**:

$$
\frac{(12k)(60k)}{12k+60k}=\frac{720M}{72k}=10\,\mathrm{k\Omega}
$$
== Current source → voltage source
VA 0,3 -> 0,0 "$150\,\mathrm{V}$"
R2 0,3 -> 3,3 "$10\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 3,3 -> 6,3
R3 6,3 -> 9,3 "$15\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 0,0 -> 9,0
terminal 9,3
terminal 9,0
label 9,3 "$A$" above
label 9,0 "$B$" below
gap 9,3 -> 9,0 v="$v_{AB}$"
--
$15\,\mathrm{mA}$ **parallel** with $10\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ → a voltage source in **series** with $10\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$:

$$
v=(15m)(10k)=150\,\mathrm{V}
$$

The current source pushed **up** → $+$ at the **top**.
== Series → Thévenin circuit
VA 0,3 -> 0,0 "$150\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 0,3 -> 3,3
RTH 3,3 -> 6,3 "$25\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 6,3 -> 9,3
wire 0,0 -> 9,0
terminal 9,3
terminal 9,0
label 9,3 "$A$" above
label 9,0 "$B$" below
gap 9,3 -> 9,0 v="$v_{AB}$"
#+ $V_{Th}=150\,\mathrm{V}$
#+ $R_{Th}=25\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$
--
$10\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ and $15\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ in series:

$$
R_{Th}=10k+15k=25\,\mathrm{k\Omega}
$$

$$
\boxed{V_{Th}=150\,\mathrm{V},\; R_{Th}=25\,\mathrm{k\Omega}}
$$

An ideal meter (no current) would read $150\,\mathrm{V}$.
== Meter on → mesh + Ohm
VA 0,3 -> 0,0 "$150\,\mathrm{V}$"
wire 0,3 -> 3,3
RTH 3,3 -> 6,3 "$25\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 6,3 -> 9,3
wire 0,0 -> 9,0
terminal 9,3
terminal 9,0
label 9,3 "$A$" above
label 9,0 "$B$" below
wire 9,3 -> 10.5,3
RM 10.5,3 -> 10.5,0 "$100\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" v="$v_{AB}$"
wire 9,0 -> 10.5,0
#= mesh 5,1.5 "$I$" cw r=0.8
#= sign 3.4,2.65 +
#= sign 5.6,2.65 -
#+ $I=1.2\,\mathrm{mA}$
#+ $v_{AB}=120\,\mathrm{V}$
--
The meter is a $100\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ load. $I$ enters it at the top → $+$ on top, same as $v_{AB}$.

KVL (sign you enter by):

$$
-150+25kI+100kI=0
$$

$$
125kI=150 \;\Rightarrow\; I=1.2\,\mathrm{mA}
$$

Ohm on the meter:

$$
v_{AB}=I\cdot100k=(1.2m)(100k)
$$

$$
\boxed{v_{AB}=120\,\mathrm{V}}
$$
```

```circuitsteps
title "Problem 17 · Thévenin: a dependent source needs a test source"
== The circuit
R1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$60\,\Omega$"
wire 0,3 -> 2,3
I1 2,0 -> 2,3 "$4\,\mathrm{A}$"
R2 2,3 -> 4,3 "$20\,\Omega$"
E1 4,3 -> 6,3 "$160i_\Delta$"
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$80\,\Omega$"
R4 9,3 -> 9,0 "$40\,\Omega$" i="$i_\Delta$"
wire 6,3 -> 9,3
wire 9,3 -> 10.5,3
wire 0,0 -> 10.5,0
terminal 10.5,3 "$a$" right
terminal 10.5,0 "$b$" right
ground 6,0
--
A dependent source $160i_\Delta$ sits inside.

**Plan**
1. $V_{Th}=V_{oc}$: tidy the left side, then mesh + Ohm.
2. $R_{Th}$: a test source (the dependent source can't be switched off).
3. Draw the Thévenin circuit.
== Source transformation
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$240\,\mathrm{V}$"
R5 0,3 -> 2,3 "$60\,\Omega$"
R2 2,3 -> 4,3 "$20\,\Omega$"
E1 4,3 -> 6,3 "$160i_\Delta$"
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$80\,\Omega$"
R4 9,3 -> 9,0 "$40\,\Omega$" i="$i_\Delta$"
wire 6,3 -> 9,3
wire 9,3 -> 10.5,3
wire 0,0 -> 10.5,0
terminal 10.5,3 "$a$" right
terminal 10.5,0 "$b$" right
ground 6,0
--
$4\,\mathrm{A}$ in parallel with $60\,\Omega$ → a voltage source in series with $60\,\Omega$:

$$
V=IR=(4)(60)=240\,\mathrm{V}
$$

The arrow pointed up → $+$ on top.
== Series: $60+20$
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$240\,\mathrm{V}$"
R6 0,3 -> 4,3 "$80\,\Omega$"
E1 4,3 -> 6,3 "$160i_\Delta$"
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$80\,\Omega$"
R4 9,3 -> 9,0 "$40\,\Omega$" i="$i_\Delta$"
wire 6,3 -> 9,3
wire 9,3 -> 10.5,3
wire 0,0 -> 10.5,0
terminal 10.5,3 "$a$" right
terminal 10.5,0 "$b$" right
ground 6,0
--
$60\,\Omega$ and $20\,\Omega$ now carry the same current → one $80\,\Omega$.
== Mesh 1
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$240\,\mathrm{V}$"
R6 0,3 -> 4,3 "$80\,\Omega$"
E1 4,3 -> 6,3 "$160i_\Delta$"
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$80\,\Omega$"
R4 9,3 -> 9,0 "$40\,\Omega$" i="$i_\Delta$"
wire 6,3 -> 9,3
wire 9,3 -> 10.5,3
wire 0,0 -> 10.5,0
terminal 10.5,3 "$a$" right
terminal 10.5,0 "$b$" right
ground 6,0
#= mesh 3,1.5 "$I_1$" cw r=0.85
#= mesh 7.5,1.5 "$I_2$" cw r=0.65
#= sign 1.2,2.62 +
#= sign 2.8,2.62 -
#= sign 5.62,2.3 +
#= sign 5.62,0.7 -
--
Two meshes, both clockwise. $i_\Delta$ runs down the $40\,\Omega$ → $i_\Delta=I_2$.

KVL around $I_1$ (sign you **enter** by):
- $240\,\mathrm{V}$: enter $-$ → $-240$
- $80\,\Omega$ (top): enter $+$ → $+80I_1$
- $160i_\Delta$: enter $+$ → $+160I_2$
- $80\,\Omega$ (shared): $+80(I_1-I_2)$

$$
160I_1+80I_2=240
$$
== Mesh 2 + solve
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$240\,\mathrm{V}$"
R6 0,3 -> 4,3 "$80\,\Omega$"
E1 4,3 -> 6,3 "$160i_\Delta$"
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$80\,\Omega$"
R4 9,3 -> 9,0 "$40\,\Omega$" i="$i_\Delta$"
wire 6,3 -> 9,3
wire 9,3 -> 10.5,3
wire 0,0 -> 10.5,0
terminal 10.5,3 "$a$" right
terminal 10.5,0 "$b$" right
ground 6,0
#= mesh 3,1.5 "$I_1$" cw r=0.85
#= mesh 7.5,1.5 "$I_2$" cw r=0.65
#= sign 6.38,0.7 +
#= sign 6.38,2.3 -
#= sign 8.62,2.3 +
#= sign 8.62,0.7 -
#+ $I_1=1.125\,\mathrm{A}$
#+ $I_2=0.75\,\mathrm{A}$
--
KVL around $I_2$:
- $80\,\Omega$ (shared): enter $+$ → $+80(I_2-I_1)$
- $40\,\Omega$: enter $+$ → $+40I_2$

$$
120I_2=80I_1 \;\Rightarrow\; I_2=\tfrac23 I_1
$$

Into mesh 1:

$$
160I_1+\tfrac{160}{3}I_1=240 \;\Rightarrow\; I_1=1.125\,\mathrm{A}
$$

$$
I_2=0.75\,\mathrm{A}
$$
== Ohm's law → $V_{Th}$
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$240\,\mathrm{V}$"
R6 0,3 -> 4,3 "$80\,\Omega$"
E1 4,3 -> 6,3 "$160i_\Delta$"
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$80\,\Omega$"
R4 9,3 -> 9,0 "$40\,\Omega$" i="$i_\Delta$"
wire 6,3 -> 9,3
wire 9,3 -> 10.5,3
wire 0,0 -> 10.5,0
terminal 10.5,3 "$a$" right
terminal 10.5,0 "$b$" right
ground 6,0
#= sign 6.38,0.7 +
#= sign 6.38,2.3 -
#= sign 8.62,2.3 +
#= sign 8.62,0.7 -
#= text 9.8,1.5 "$30\,\mathrm{V}$" color=pink
#+ $V_{Th}=30\,\mathrm{V}$
--
$a$–$b$ sits right across the $40\,\Omega$. $I_2$ enters it at the top → $+$ at $a$.

$$
V_{Th}=40I_2=(40)(0.75)=30\,\mathrm{V}
$$
== Sources off
wire 0,3 -> 0,0
R6 0,3 -> 4,3 "$80\,\Omega$"
E1 4,3 -> 6,3 "$160i_\Delta$"
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$80\,\Omega$"
R4 9,3 -> 9,0 "$40\,\Omega$" i="$i_\Delta$"
wire 6,3 -> 9,3
wire 9,3 -> 10.5,3
wire 0,0 -> 10.5,0
terminal 10.5,3 "$a$" right
terminal 10.5,0 "$b$" right
ground 6,0
--
Independent sources off: $240\,\mathrm{V}$ → **wire** (same as opening the $4\,\mathrm{A}$ in the original: $60+20$ stays in series).

The dependent source **stays on**: it is controlled by $i_\Delta$, which is still there.
== Test source
wire 0,3 -> 0,0
R6 0,3 -> 4,3 "$80\,\Omega$"
E1 4,3 -> 6,3 "$160i_\Delta$"
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$80\,\Omega$"
R4 9,3 -> 9,0 "$40\,\Omega$" i="$i_\Delta$"
wire 6,3 -> 9,3
wire 9,3 -> 10.5,3
wire 0,0 -> 10.5,0
terminal 10.5,3 "$a$" right
terminal 10.5,0 "$b$" right
ground 6,0
V9 10.5,3 -> 10.5,0 "$1\,\mathrm{V}$"
--
Put $1\,\mathrm{V}$ across $a$–$b$ and find the current $i_T$ it pushes in.

$$
R_{Th}=\frac{1\,\mathrm{V}}{i_T}
$$
== Ohm's law per branch
wire 0,3 -> 0,0
R6 0,3 -> 4,3 "$80\,\Omega$"
E1 4,3 -> 6,3 "$160i_\Delta$"
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$80\,\Omega$"
R4 9,3 -> 9,0 "$40\,\Omega$" i="$i_\Delta$"
wire 6,3 -> 9,3
wire 9,3 -> 10.5,3
wire 0,0 -> 10.5,0
terminal 10.5,3 "$a$" right
terminal 10.5,0 "$b$" right
ground 6,0
V9 10.5,3 -> 10.5,0 "$1\,\mathrm{V}$"
#= text 9.75,0.45 "$25\,\mathrm{mA}$" color=pink
#= text 7,0.45 "$12.5\,\mathrm{mA}$" color=pink
#= text 2,2.35 "$62.5\,\mathrm{mA}$" color=pink
#+ $R_{Th}=10\,\Omega$
--
Every branch runs from $a$ (1 V) to ground:
- $40\,\Omega$: $i_\Delta=\frac{1}{40}=25\,\mathrm{mA}$
- $80\,\Omega$: $\frac{1}{80}=12.5\,\mathrm{mA}$
- left: the source lifts it to $1+160i_\Delta=1+4=5\,\mathrm{V}$, so $\frac{5}{80}=62.5\,\mathrm{mA}$

KCL at $a$ (entering $+$, leaving $-$):

$$
i_T-25m-12.5m-62.5m=0 \;\Rightarrow\; i_T=100\,\mathrm{mA}
$$

$$
R_{Th}=\frac{1}{100m}=10\,\Omega
$$
== Thévenin circuit
V7 0,3 -> 0,0 "$30\,\mathrm{V}$"
R7 0,3 -> 4,3 "$10\,\Omega$"
wire 4,3 -> 10.5,3
wire 0,0 -> 10.5,0
terminal 10.5,3 "$a$" right
terminal 10.5,0 "$b$" right
--
$$
\boxed{V_{Th}=30\,\mathrm{V},\quad R_{Th}=10\,\Omega}
$$

Any load on $a$–$b$ now sees just this.
```

```circuitsteps
title "Problem 18 · Norton: a shorted internal branch"
== The circuit
I1 0,0 -> 0,4 "$15\,\mathrm{A}$"
wire 0,4 -> 3,4
R1 3,4 -> 3,0 "$8\,\Omega$"
R2 3,4 -> 6,4 "$2\,\Omega$"
R3 6,4 -> 6,0 "$12\,\Omega$"
wire 6,4 -> 9,4
terminal 9,4 "$a$" right
wire 0,0 -> 3,0
R4 3,0 -> 6,0 "$10\,\Omega$"
wire 6,0 -> 9,0
terminal 9,0 "$b$" right
label 3,4 "$p$" above
label 3,0 "$q$" below
ground 6,0
--
Norton equivalent = current source $I_N$ in parallel with $R_N$.

**Plan**
1. $I_N$: short $a$–$b$, find the current in the short.
2. $R_N$: source off, look in from $a$–$b$.
3. Draw $I_N \parallel R_N$.
== Short $a$–$b$
I1 0,0 -> 0,4 "$15\,\mathrm{A}$"
wire 0,4 -> 3,4
wire 0,0 -> 3,0
R1 3,4 -> 3,0 "$8\,\Omega$"
R2 3,4 -> 6,4 "$2\,\Omega$"
R3 6,4 -> 6,0 "$12\,\Omega$"
R4 3,0 -> 6,0 "$10\,\Omega$"
wire 6,4 -> 9,4
terminal 9,4 "$a$" right
wire 6,0 -> 9,0
terminal 9,0 "$b$" right
label 3,4 "$p$" above
label 3,0 "$q$" below
ground 6,0
wire 9,4 -> 9,0
--
A wire from $a$ to $b$. The current in it is $I_N$.

The $12\,\Omega$ now sits right across the short → $0\,\mathrm{V}$ across it → **no current** in it.
== Mesh currents
I1 0,0 -> 0,4 "$15\,\mathrm{A}$"
wire 0,4 -> 3,4
wire 0,0 -> 3,0
R1 3,4 -> 3,0 "$8\,\Omega$"
R2 3,4 -> 6,4 "$2\,\Omega$"
R3 6,4 -> 6,0 "$12\,\Omega$"
R4 3,0 -> 6,0 "$10\,\Omega$"
wire 6,4 -> 9,4
terminal 9,4 "$a$" right
wire 6,0 -> 9,0
terminal 9,0 "$b$" right
label 3,4 "$p$" above
label 3,0 "$q$" below
ground 6,0
wire 9,4 -> 9,0
#= mesh 1.4,2 "$I_1$" cw r=0.6
#= mesh 4.5,2 "$I_2$" cw r=0.75
#+ $I_1=15\,\mathrm{A}$
--
Two windows carry current: $I_1$ (left) and $I_2$ (middle), both clockwise.

The $15\,\mathrm{A}$ source sits only in mesh 1, pointing the same way:

$$
I_1=15\,\mathrm{A}
$$
== Signs + KVL on mesh 2
I1 0,0 -> 0,4 "$15\,\mathrm{A}$"
wire 0,4 -> 3,4
wire 0,0 -> 3,0
R1 3,4 -> 3,0 "$8\,\Omega$"
R2 3,4 -> 6,4 "$2\,\Omega$"
R3 6,4 -> 6,0 "$12\,\Omega$"
R4 3,0 -> 6,0 "$10\,\Omega$"
wire 6,4 -> 9,4
terminal 9,4 "$a$" right
wire 6,0 -> 9,0
terminal 9,0 "$b$" right
label 3,4 "$p$" above
label 3,0 "$q$" below
ground 6,0
wire 9,4 -> 9,0
#= mesh 1.4,2 "$I_1$" cw r=0.6
#= mesh 4.5,2 "$I_2$" cw r=0.75
#= sign 3.35,1.25 +
#= sign 3.35,2.75 -
#= sign 3.6,3.62 +
#= sign 5.4,3.62 -
#= sign 5.4,0.38 +
#= sign 3.6,0.38 -
#+ $I_2=6\,\mathrm{A}$
--
$+$ where $I_2$ **enters** each resistor. The $8\,\Omega$ is shared: it carries $I_2-I_1$.
- $8\,\Omega$: $+8(I_2-I_1)$
- $2\,\Omega$: $+2I_2$
- short: no voltage
- $10\,\Omega$: $+10I_2$

$$
8(I_2-15)+2I_2+10I_2=0
$$

$$
20I_2=120 \;\Rightarrow\; I_2=6\,\mathrm{A}
$$
== $I_N$ = current in the short
I1 0,0 -> 0,4 "$15\,\mathrm{A}$"
wire 0,4 -> 3,4
wire 0,0 -> 3,0
R1 3,4 -> 3,0 "$8\,\Omega$"
R2 3,4 -> 6,4 "$2\,\Omega$"
R3 6,4 -> 6,0 "$12\,\Omega$"
R4 3,0 -> 6,0 "$10\,\Omega$"
wire 6,4 -> 9,4
terminal 9,4 "$a$" right
wire 6,0 -> 9,0
terminal 9,0 "$b$" right
label 3,4 "$p$" above
label 3,0 "$q$" below
ground 6,0
wire 9,4 -> 9,0
#= path 6.6,4 -> 9,4 -> 9,0.6 "$6\,\mathrm{A}$"
#+ $I_N=6\,\mathrm{A}$
--
The short is on mesh 2's right side, so its current is $I_2$, flowing $a \to b$:

$$
\boxed{I_N=6\,\mathrm{A}}
$$

In the Norton circuit, this current comes **out of the top** of the source into $a$.
== $R_N$: source off
R1 3,4 -> 3,0 "$8\,\Omega$"
R2 3,4 -> 6,4 "$2\,\Omega$"
R3 6,4 -> 6,0 "$12\,\Omega$"
R4 3,0 -> 6,0 "$10\,\Omega$"
wire 6,4 -> 9,4
terminal 9,4 "$a$" right
wire 6,0 -> 9,0
terminal 9,0 "$b$" right
label 3,4 "$p$" above
label 3,0 "$q$" below
ground 6,0
#= path 10.6,2 -> 9.3,2 thin color=accent
#= text 10.1,2.45 "$R_N$" color=accent
#+ $R_N=7.5\,\Omega$
--
Current source off = **open** (it disappears).

From $a$: the $12\,\Omega$ goes straight to $b$.

The other way: $2\,\Omega$ → $p$ → $8\,\Omega$ → $q$ → $10\,\Omega$ → $b$, all in **series**: $20\,\Omega$.

$$
R_N=12\parallel 20=\frac{(12)(20)}{12+20}=7.5\,\Omega
$$
== Norton circuit
IN 4,0 -> 4,4 "$6\,\mathrm{A}$"
RN 6.5,4 -> 6.5,0 "$7.5\,\Omega$"
wire 4,4 -> 9,4
terminal 9,4 "$a$" right
wire 4,0 -> 9,0
terminal 9,0 "$b$" right
--
$$
\boxed{I_N=6\,\mathrm{A}\ (\text{up, into } a)\;\parallel\;R_N=7.5\,\Omega}
$$

**Check** ($a$–$b$ open, mesh 2 now goes through the $12\,\Omega$):

$$
8(I_2-15)+2I_2+12I_2+10I_2=0 \;\Rightarrow\; I_2=3.75\,\mathrm{A}
$$

$$
V_{oc}=12(3.75)=45\,\mathrm{V}=I_NR_N=(6)(7.5)
$$

✓ Same circuit.
```

```circuitsteps
- $15\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$: enter $+$ → $+15kI_A$
- $5\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$: enter $+$ → $+5k(I_B-I_C)=0$

$$

I1 0,0 -> 0,3 "$10\,\mathrm{mA}$"
R1 2,3 -> 2,0 "$10\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"

$$

$$

The short is $I_C$'s right side ($a \to b$), and $I_C=I_B$:

$$
\boxed{I_N=i_{sc}=-1\,\mathrm{mA}}
$$

Negative: $1\,\mathrm{mA}$ really flows **up** the short, $b \to a$.
== $R_N$: sources off
wire 0,3 -> 4,3
wire 4,3 -> 4,0
R1 2,3 -> 2,0 "$10\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R2 4,3 -> 7,3 "$15\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"

$$
\boxed{1\,\mathrm{mA}\ (\text{down, toward } b)\;\parallel\;R_N=3.75\,\mathrm{k\Omega}}
$$

$$

$$
V_{oc}=5kI_B=-3.75\,\mathrm{V}=I_NR_N=(-1m)(3.75k)\;✓
```

```circuitsteps
title "Problem 20 · Norton: a dependent source stays on"
== The circuit
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$280\,\mathrm{V}$"

Norton equivalent = current source $I_N$ in parallel with $R_N$.

The $0.2i_\Delta$ source is **dependent**: it can't be turned off. So:

**Plan**
1. $I_N$: short $a$–$b$, find the current in the short.
2. $V_{oc}$: terminals open.
3. $R_N=V_{oc}/I_N$, then draw $I_N \parallel R_N$.

V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$280\,\mathrm{V}$"

--
A wire from $a$ to $b$. The current in it is $I_N$.

The $5.6\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ sits right across the short → **no current** in it.
== Mesh currents
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$280\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_\Delta$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"

terminal 8,0 "$b$" right
wire 8,3 -> 8,0

#= mesh 4.1,1.5 "$I_2$" cw r=0.5
#= mesh 4.5,4.35 "$I_3$" cw r=0.4

Three windows, all clockwise: $I_1$ (left), $I_2$ (right, through the short), $I_3$ (top, holds the dependent source).

$i_\Delta$ is the current in the left $2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$, the same way as $I_1$:

$$
i_\Delta=I_1
$$

The $0.2i_\Delta$ source sits only in mesh 3, pointing the same way (right along the top):

$$
I_3=0.2i_\Delta=0.2I_1
$$
== KVL on mesh 1
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$280\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_\Delta$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R3 3,3 -> 6,3 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"

#= mesh 4.1,1.5 "$I_2$" cw r=0.5
#= mesh 4.5,4.35 "$I_3$" cw r=0.4

#= sign 2.4,2.62 -
#= sign 2.65,2.3 +
#= sign 2.65,0.7 -
--
$+$ where $I_1$ **enters** each element:
- $280\,\mathrm{V}$: enter $-$ → $-280$
- top $2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$: $+2kI_1$
- middle $2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ (shared): $+2k(I_1-I_2)$

$$
-280+2kI_1+2k(I_1-I_2)=0
$$

$$
4kI_1-2kI_2=280
$$
== KVL on mesh 2
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$280\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_\Delta$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"

#= mesh 4.1,1.5 "$I_2$" cw r=0.5
#= mesh 4.5,4.35 "$I_3$" cw r=0.4
#= sign 3.35,0.7 +
#= sign 3.35,2.3 -
#= sign 3.6,2.62 +
#= sign 5.4,2.62 -
--
$+$ where $I_2$ **enters** each element:
- middle $2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ (shared with mesh 1): $+2k(I_2-I_1)$
- right $2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ (shared with mesh 3): $+2k(I_2-I_3)$
- short: no voltage

$$
2k(I_2-I_1)+2k(I_2-0.2I_1)=0
$$

$$
4kI_2=2.4kI_1 \;\Rightarrow\; I_2=0.6I_1
$$
== Solve → $I_N$
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$280\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_\Delta$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R3 3,3 -> 6,3 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 3,3 -> 3,5.2
F1 3,5.2 -> 6,5.2 "$0.2i_\Delta$"
wire 6,5.2 -> 6,3
R4 6,3 -> 6,0 "$5.6\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 6,3 -> 8,3
terminal 8,3 "$a$" right
wire 0,0 -> 8,0
terminal 8,0 "$b$" right
wire 8,3 -> 8,0
#= mesh 1.5,1.5 "$I_1$" cw r=0.6
#= mesh 4.1,1.5 "$I_2$" cw r=0.5
#= mesh 4.5,4.35 "$I_3$" cw r=0.4
#= path 6.6,3 -> 8,3 -> 8,0.6 "$60\,\mathrm{mA}$"
#+ $I_N=60\,\mathrm{mA}$
--
Put $I_2=0.6I_1$ into mesh 1:

$$
4kI_1-1.2kI_1=280 \;\Rightarrow\; I_1=\frac{280}{2.8k}=100\,\mathrm{mA}
$$

$$
I_2=0.6(100m)=60\,\mathrm{mA}
$$

The short carries $I_2$, flowing $a\to b$:

$$
\boxed{I_N=60\,\mathrm{mA}}
$$
== Open $a$–$b$: $V_{oc}$
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$280\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,3 -> 3,3 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_\Delta$"
R2 3,3 -> 3,0 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R3 3,3 -> 6,3 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 3,3 -> 3,5.2
F1 3,5.2 -> 6,5.2 "$0.2i_\Delta$"
wire 6,5.2 -> 6,3
R4 6,3 -> 6,0 "$5.6\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 6,3 -> 8,3
terminal 8,3 "$a$" right
wire 0,0 -> 8,0
terminal 8,0 "$b$" right
#= mesh 1.5,1.5 "$I_1$" cw r=0.6
#= mesh 4.1,1.5 "$I_2$" cw r=0.5
#= mesh 4.5,4.35 "$I_3$" cw r=0.4
#= sign 3.35,0.7 +
#= sign 3.35,2.3 -
#= sign 3.6,2.62 +
#= sign 5.4,2.62 -
#= sign 5.65,2.3 +
#= sign 5.65,0.7 -
#+ $V_{oc}=112\,\mathrm{V}$
--
Short removed: mesh 2 now goes down through the $5.6\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ (enter $+$ → $+5.6kI_2$).

Mesh 2:

$$
2k(I_2-I_1)+2k(I_2-0.2I_1)+5.6kI_2=0 \;\Rightarrow\; I_2=0.25I_1
$$

Mesh 1 is unchanged:

$$
4kI_1-2k(0.25I_1)=280 \;\Rightarrow\; I_1=80\,\mathrm{mA},\quad I_2=20\,\mathrm{mA}
$$

Ohm's law on the $5.6\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$:

$$
V_{oc}=(20m)(5.6k)=112\,\mathrm{V}
$$
== Norton circuit
IN 4,0 -> 4,3 "$60\,\mathrm{mA}$"
RN 6,3 -> 6,0 "$1.867\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
wire 4,3 -> 8,3
terminal 8,3 "$a$" right
wire 4,0 -> 8,0
terminal 8,0 "$b$" right
#+ $R_N=1866.67\,\Omega$
--
$$
R_N=\frac{V_{oc}}{I_N}=\frac{112}{60m}=1866.67\,\Omega
$$

$$
\boxed{I_N=60\,\mathrm{mA}\ (\text{up, into } a)\;\parallel\;R_N=1866.67\,\Omega}
$$
```

```circuitsteps
**Plan**
1. $V_{Th}$: $a$–$b$ open, KCL at $a$.

3. Norton: short $a$–$b$.
4. Max power: $R_o=R_{Th}$.
5. Efficiency: put $R_o$ on the original circuit.

- $4\,\mathrm{A}$ → **open**

wire 0,3 -> 0,5

#+ $R_{Th}=1\,\Omega$

KCL at $a$ (entering $+$, leaving $-$):

$$

$$

$$
i_T=\frac{4v_T+3v_T+v_T}{8}=v_T
$$

$$
\boxed{R_{Th}=\frac{v_T}{i_T}=1\,\Omega}
$$

$$
\frac{24-0}{2}=12\,\mathrm{A}\ \text{into } a
$$

$4\,\mathrm{A}$ leaves through the source; the rest goes down the short:

$$
\boxed{I_N=12-4=8\,\mathrm{A}}
$$

RN 7,3 -> 7,0 "$1\,\Omega$"
wire 5,3 -> 9,3
wire 5,0 -> 9,0
terminal 9,3 "$a$" right
terminal 9,0 "$b$" right

$$

$$

#= sign 8.65,2.3 +
#= sign 8.65,0.7 -

Mesh on the Thévenin circuit:

$$

$$

$$
\boxed{P_{max}=I^2R_o=(4)^2(1)=16\,\mathrm{W}}
$$

$V_a=IR_o=4\,\mathrm{V}$ (half of $V_{Th}$).

$$

$$
i_1=\frac{24-4}{2}=10\,\mathrm{A}\ \text{(into } a)
$$

KCL at the $24\,\mathrm{V}$ node: $1.5\,\mathrm{A}$ arrives from $3i_x$, $10\,\mathrm{A}$ leaves through the $2\,\Omega$:

$$
```

```schematic
R3 6,4 -> 8,4 "$8\,\Omega$"
```

```circuitsteps
8(I_2-I_3)-20(I_1-I_3)+2I_2+40(I_2-I_1)=0

Going with $I_3$: top $4\,\Omega$, then back along the $8\,\Omega$ and $6\,\Omega$:

$$
4I_3+8(I_3-I_2)+6(I_3-I_1)=0
$$

All three in standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}50I_1-40I_2-6I_3&=-480\\-60I_1+50I_2+12I_3&=0\\-6I_1-8I_2+18I_3&=0\end{aligned}
$$

Solve: $I_1=-99.6\,\mathrm{A}$, $I_2=-100.8\,\mathrm{A}$, $I_3=-78\,\mathrm{A}$.
== Walk to $V_{oc}$
V1 0,0 -> 0,4 "$480\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 0,4 -> 4,4 "$6\,\Omega$" i="$i_\beta$"
R3 6,4 -> 8,4 "$8\,\Omega$"

#= path 5,4 -> 4,4 -> 4,0 -> 4.85,0
#+ $V_{Th}=48\,\mathrm{V}$

Walk from $p$ down the $40\,\Omega$ to ground. Down it flows $I_1-I_2=1.2\,\mathrm{A}$ → enter $+$:

$$
V_{oc}=40(I_1-I_2)=40(1.2)=48\,\mathrm{V}
$$
== Short $p$ to ground

R1 0,4 -> 4,4 "$6\,\Omega$" i="$i_\beta$"
R3 6,4 -> 8,4 "$8\,\Omega$"

#= mesh 6.3,2 "$I_2$" cw r=0.65
#= mesh 5.5,5.15 "$I_3$" cw r=0.42
#+ $I_{sc}=4\,\mathrm{A}$

The short puts both ends of the $40\,\Omega$ at $0\,\mathrm{V}$ → no current: drop it. Same meshes, no $40$ terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}10I_1-6I_3&=-480\\-20I_1+10I_2+12I_3&=0\\-6I_1-8I_2+18I_3&=0\end{aligned}
$$

Solve: $I_1=-92\,\mathrm{A}$, $I_2=-96\,\mathrm{A}$, $I_3=-73.3\,\mathrm{A}$.

Down the short: $I_{sc}=I_1-I_2=4\,\mathrm{A}$.
== Thévenin circuit, matched load
VTH 0,4 -> 0,0 "$48\,\mathrm{V}$"
RTH 0,4 -> 3,4 "$12\,\Omega$"
wire 3,4 -> 5,4
RL 5,4 -> 5,0 "$R_L=12\,\Omega$"

#= mesh 2.2,2 "$I$" cw r=0.8

#+ $p_{max}=48\,\mathrm{W}$

$$
R_{Th}=\frac{V_{oc}}{I_{sc}}=\frac{48}{4}=12\,\Omega
$$

Max power → $R_L=12\,\Omega$. KVL with $I$:

$$
-48+12I+12I=0\;\Rightarrow\;I=2\,\mathrm{A}
$$

$$
p_{max}=I^2R_L=(2)^2(12)=48\,\mathrm{W}
$$
```

```circuitsteps
title "Problem 24 · Superposition with three sources"
== The circuit
I1 0,0 -> 0,4 "$6\,\mathrm{A}$"
wire 0,4 -> 2,4

--
Three independent sources → three small problems, then add.

**Turning a source off**
- voltage source → **wire**
- current source → **open** (it disappears)
== $6\,\mathrm{A}$ alone
I1 0,0 -> 0,4 "$6\,\mathrm{A}$"
wire 0,4 -> 2,4
R1 2,4 -> 2,0 "$20\,\Omega$"
R2 2,4 -> 4.5,4 "$1\,\Omega$" i="$i_o$"

wire 0,0 -> 10.5,0
label 1.1,4 "$p$" above
label 4.5,4 "$q$" above
label 8.5,2 "$k$" right
ground 0,0
--
$10\,\mathrm{A}$ off → open. $75\,\mathrm{V}$ off → wire.

Now the $60\,\Omega$, $5\,\Omega$ and $30\,\Omega$ all run from $q$ to ground → **parallel**:

$$
\frac{1}{60}+\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{30}=\frac{1+12+2}{60}=\frac{1}{4}
$$

So they act like one $4\,\Omega$.
== $6\,\mathrm{A}$ alone: mesh
I1 0,0 -> 0,4 "$6\,\mathrm{A}$"
wire 0,4 -> 2,4
R1 2,4 -> 2,0 "$20\,\Omega$"
R2 2,4 -> 4.5,4 "$1\,\Omega$" i="$i_o$"
REQ 7.5,4 -> 7.5,0 "$4\,\Omega$"
wire 4.5,4 -> 7.5,4

label 4.5,4 "$q$" above
ground 0,0
#= mesh 1,1.1 "$I_1$" cw r=0.45
#= mesh 4.6,2 "$I_2$" cw r=0.8
#= sign 2.35,1.2 +
#= sign 2.35,2.8 -
#= sign 2.5,3.62 +
#= sign 4.0,3.62 -
#= sign 7.15,2.8 +
#= sign 7.15,1.2 -
#+ $i_o{}^{\prime}=4.8\,\mathrm{A}$
--
Mesh 1 holds the $6\,\mathrm{A}$ source (same direction): $I_1=6\,\mathrm{A}$.

Mesh 2 (signs you enter by; the $20\,\Omega$ carries $I_2-I_1$):

$$
20(I_2-6)+1I_2+4I_2=0
$$

$$
25I_2=120 \;\Rightarrow\; I_2=4.8\,\mathrm{A}
$$

$i_o$ is mesh 2's top current: $i_o{}^{\prime}=4.8\,\mathrm{A}$.
== $10\,\mathrm{A}$ alone
wire 0,4 -> 2,4
R1 2,4 -> 2,0 "$20\,\Omega$"
R2 2,4 -> 4.5,4 "$1\,\Omega$" i="$i_o$"
I2 4.5,4 -> 4.5,0 "$10\,\mathrm{A}$"
wire 4.5,4 -> 10.5,4

R4 8.5,4 -> 8.5,2 "$5\,\Omega$"
wire 8.5,2 -> 8.5,0
R5 10.5,4 -> 10.5,0 "$30\,\Omega$"

label 1.1,4 "$p$" above
label 4.5,4 "$q$" above
label 8.5,2 "$k$" right
ground 0,0
--
$6\,\mathrm{A}$ off → open. $75\,\mathrm{V}$ off → wire.

Same $60\parallel5\parallel30=4\,\Omega$ on the right.
== $10\,\mathrm{A}$ alone: supermesh
wire 0,4 -> 2,4
R1 2,4 -> 2,0 "$20\,\Omega$"
R2 2,4 -> 4.5,4 "$1\,\Omega$" i="$i_o$"
I2 4.5,4 -> 4.5,0 "$10\,\mathrm{A}$"
REQ 7.5,4 -> 7.5,0 "$4\,\Omega$"
wire 4.5,4 -> 7.5,4
wire 0,0 -> 7.5,0
label 1.1,4 "$p$" above
label 4.5,4 "$q$" above
ground 0,0
#= mesh 3.0,1.6 "$I_A$" cw r=0.5
#= mesh 5.85,1.5 "$I_B$" cw r=0.45
#= region 1.55,-0.8 7.95,4.45 "supermesh"
#= sign 2.35,1.2 +
#= sign 2.35,2.8 -
#= sign 2.5,3.62 +
#= sign 4.0,3.62 -
#= sign 7.15,2.8 +
#= sign 7.15,1.2 -
#+ $i_o{}^{\prime\prime}=1.6\,\mathrm{A}$
--
The $10\,\mathrm{A}$ source is shared by meshes $A$ and $B$ → **supermesh** (walk around the outside).

Source constraint (down the source: $I_A$ down, $I_B$ up):

$$
I_A-I_B=10
$$

KVL around the outside:

$$
20I_A+1I_A+4I_B=0
$$

Substitute $I_B=I_A-10$:

$$
25I_A=40 \;\Rightarrow\; I_A=1.6\,\mathrm{A}
$$

$i_o{}^{\prime\prime}=I_A=1.6\,\mathrm{A}$.
== $75\,\mathrm{V}$ alone
wire 0,4 -> 2,4
R1 2,4 -> 2,0 "$20\,\Omega$"
R2 2,4 -> 4.5,4 "$1\,\Omega$" i="$i_o$"
wire 4.5,4 -> 10.5,4
R3 6.5,4 -> 6.5,0 "$60\,\Omega$"
R4 8.5,4 -> 8.5,2 "$5\,\Omega$"
V1 8.5,2 -> 8.5,0 "$75\,\mathrm{V}$"
R5 10.5,4 -> 10.5,0 "$30\,\Omega$"
wire 0,0 -> 10.5,0
label 1.1,4 "$p$" above
label 4.5,4 "$q$" above
label 8.5,2 "$k$" right
ground 0,0
--
Both current sources off → open.

$20\,\Omega$ and $1\,\Omega$ are now in **series** from $q$ to ground ($21\,\Omega$), and $i_o$ flows through them.

Only one unknown node, $q$ → **nodal** is quickest.
== $75\,\mathrm{V}$ alone: nodal at $q$
wire 0,4 -> 2,4
R1 2,4 -> 2,0 "$20\,\Omega$"
R2 2,4 -> 4.5,4 "$1\,\Omega$"
wire 4.5,4 -> 10.5,4
dot 4.5,4
R3 6.5,4 -> 6.5,0 "$60\,\Omega$" i="$i_3$"
R4 8.5,4 -> 8.5,2 "$5\,\Omega$" i="$i_4$"
V1 8.5,2 -> 8.5,0 "$75\,\mathrm{V}$"
R5 10.5,4 -> 10.5,0 "$30\,\Omega$" i="$i_5$"
wire 0,0 -> 10.5,0
label 1.1,4 "$p$" above
label 4.5,4 "$q$" above
label 8.5,2 "$k$" right
ground 0,0
#= path 4.2,3.6 -> 2.35,3.6 -> 2.35,0.4 thin color=orange
#= text 3.3,2.2 "$i_{21}$" color=orange
#+ $i_o{}^{\prime\prime\prime}=-2.4\,\mathrm{A}$
--
Currents leaving $q$ toward ground ((start − end)/R; $V_k=75\,\mathrm{V}$):

$$
-\frac{V_q-0}{21}-\frac{V_q-0}{60}-\frac{V_q-75}{5}-\frac{V_q-0}{30}=0
$$

Multiply by $-420$:

$$
20V_q+7V_q+84(V_q-75)+14V_q=0 \;\Rightarrow\; 125V_q=6300
$$

$$
V_q=50.4\,\mathrm{V} \qquad i_{21}=\frac{50.4}{21}=2.4\,\mathrm{A}\ (q\to p)
$$

$i_o$ points $p\to q$, so $i_o{}^{\prime\prime\prime}=-2.4\,\mathrm{A}$.
== Add the three
I1 0,0 -> 0,4 "$6\,\mathrm{A}$"
wire 0,4 -> 2,4
R1 2,4 -> 2,0 "$20\,\Omega$"
R2 2,4 -> 4.5,4 "$1\,\Omega$" i="$i_o$"
I2 4.5,4 -> 4.5,0 "$10\,\mathrm{A}$"
wire 4.5,4 -> 10.5,4
R3 6.5,4 -> 6.5,0 "$60\,\Omega$"
R4 8.5,4 -> 8.5,2 "$5\,\Omega$"
V1 8.5,2 -> 8.5,0 "$75\,\mathrm{V}$"
R5 10.5,4 -> 10.5,0 "$30\,\Omega$"
wire 0,0 -> 10.5,0
label 1.1,4 "$p$" above
label 4.5,4 "$q$" above
label 8.5,2 "$k$" right
ground 0,0
#+ $i_o=4\,\mathrm{A}$
--
$$
i_o=i_o{}^{\prime}+i_o{}^{\prime\prime}+i_o{}^{\prime\prime\prime}=4.8+1.6-2.4
$$

$$
\boxed{i_o=4\,\mathrm{A}}
$$

Add currents and voltages only, **never powers**.
```

```circuitsteps
$$

wire 0,3 -> 0,0
R1 3,3 -> 3,0 "$5\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R2 3,3 -> 6,3 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$6\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_o$"

--
Signs you **enter** by, going with $I_A$:

$$
2k(I_A-I_B)+6kI_A=0
$$

$$
8kI_A=2kI_B=2k(-5m)=-10\;\Rightarrow\;I_A=-1.25\,\mathrm{mA}
$$

$I_A$ is the only current down the $6\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ → $i_o''=-1.25\,\mathrm{mA}$.

wire 6,5 -> 6,3
wire 0,3 -> 3,3
wire 6,3 -> 9,3
wire 0,0 -> 9,0
label 3,3 "$a$" below
label 6,3 "$b$" below
ground 0,0
#+ $i_o=2.25\,\mathrm{mA}$
--
$$
i_o=i_o'+i_o''=3.5+(-1.25)=2.25\,\mathrm{mA}
$$
== Check: all three on
V1 0,3 -> 0,0 "$8\,\mathrm{V}$"
R1 3,3 -> 3,0 "$5\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R2 3,3 -> 6,3 "$2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$"
R3 6,3 -> 6,0 "$6\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$" i="$i_o$"

I2 6,5 -> 3,5 "$5\,\mathrm{mA}$"
wire 6,5 -> 6,3
wire 0,3 -> 3,3

wire 0,0 -> 9,0

label 6,3 "$b$" below

#= mesh 4.15,1.5 "$I_A$" cw r=0.6
#= mesh 4.5,4.25 "$I_B$" cw r=0.38
#= mesh 7.5,1.5 "$I_C$" cw r=0.7

$I_B=-5\,\mathrm{mA}$; the $10\,\mathrm{mA}$ points up, clockwise goes down → $I_C=-10\,\mathrm{mA}$.

- Mesh $I_A$: $5k(I_A-I_0)+2k(I_A-I_B)+6k(I_A-I_C)=0$

$$

$$

$$
i_o=I_A-I_C=-7.75+10=2.25\,\mathrm{mA}\;✓
$$
```
